# Quick Start Reference Guide

## Purpose
Get a new Quarto book from idea → local WSL project → GitHub → published website.

## Before You Start
 - Decide the book title
 - Choose repository name
 - Decide public/private GitHub repository
 - Decide where the book will live locally
 - Confirm Git, WSL/Ubuntu, VS Code, and Quarto are available

### Prerequisites
 - WSL / Ubuntu installed
 - Git installed
 - Quarto installed
 - VS Code + WSL extension
 - GitHub account
 - Git authentication configured

## Create the GitHub Repository
 - Create repository
 - Copy repository URL
 - Decide main branch
 - Clone repository into WSL

## Set Up the WSL Project
```bash
~/projects/
    └── my-new-book/
```
Commands for:

 - Creating/navigating directories
```bash
cd ~/projects
```
 - Cloning repository
```bash
git clone <github-repository-url>
cd <repository-name>
```
 - Checking Git status
```bash
git status
```
 - Opening project in VS Code
```bash
code .
```

## Create the Quarto Book
 - Initialize Quarto project
 - Understand the generated files
 - Configure _quarto.yml
 - Establish chapter structure

## Build the Book Locally
 - Preview
 ```bash
 quarto preview
 ```
 - Render
 ```bash
 quarto render
 ```
 - Check navigation, links, images, code, references

## Git Workflow
A simple repeatable workflow:
```{mermaid}
flowchart TD

    subgraph Row1[" "]
        direction LR
        pull[git pull] --> edit[edit] --> preview[quarto preview] --> Render[quarto render]
    end

    Render --> status[git status]

    subgraph Row2[" "]
        direction RL
        status --> add[git add .] --> commit[git commit] --> push[git push]
    end

    style Row1 fill:none,stroke:none
    style Row2 fill:none,stroke:none
```
## Publish with GitHub Pages
 - Configure GitHub Pages
 - Set up Quarto/GitHub Actions
 - Push changes
```bash
quarto publish
```
 - Verify published site
 - Understand what happens after each subsequent git push

## Recommended Project Structure
```bash
    my-new-book/
    ├── _quarto.yml
    ├── index.qmd
    ├── references.qmd
    ├── chapters/
    ├── images/
    ├── code/
    ├── data/
    ├── references.bib
    ├── README.md
    └── .gitignore
```
## Troubleshooting Quick Reference
| Problem                           | First thing to check                         |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `quarto: command not found`       | Is Quarto installed in WSL?                  |
| Git push fails                    | `git status`, remote URL, authentication     |
| Book doesn't render               | Run `quarto render` and read the first error |
| Image doesn't appear              | Check relative path/case                     |
| GitHub Pages not updating         | Check GitHub Actions                         |
| VS Code editing wrong environment | Confirm **WSL: Ubuntu**                      |
| Changes aren't being pushed       | `git status`                                 |

## The 5-Minute Cheat Sheet
```bash
# Clone
git clone <repo-url>
cd <repo>

# Create Quarto book
quarto create-project . --type book

# Get into your project
cd ~/projects/my-book

# Preview
quarto preview

# Verify the complete book
quarto render

# Save changes
git add .
git commit -m "Update book"
git push

# Publish the book
quarto publish
```

Quarto will guide you through the publishing destination the first time
